title: Safeguards against Volatility of Energy Prices under Revised Electricity Market Structure
what_it_is: Safeguards against Volatility of Energy Prices under Revised Electricity Market Structure

sections.label: EMA electricity market changes
sections.summary: EMA will introduce centralised generation tenders, make emergency fuel measures permanent, enhance retailer rules and tighten wholesale plan eligibility from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: First, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) will introduce a centralised approach to facilitate investments in new generation through a competitive tender to ensure that we continue to have sufficient generation capacity in time to come.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Second, EMA will institutionalise some of the emergency measures that we had introduced late last year in the wake of the global energy crisis, as permanent features of our market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: These are regulations requiring our gencos to maintain sufficient fuel for power generation and the standby fuel facility to guard against risks of gas supply disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: EMA will also be working with the industry to explore ways to aggregate gas procurement and obtain longer-term, more secure contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Third, EMA will also enhance the regulatory requirements imposed on electricity retailers, to ensure that they are sufficiently prepared and better able to withstand market volatilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: EMA will also look into tightening the eligibility criteria for consumers on Wholesale Electricity Price plans, so that only the larger consumers who are better equipped to deal with the risks of price volatilities would be allowed to enter into such plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: EMA will be consulting the industry and the public on the details of these proposed changes in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: We plan to implement these enhancements progressively from 2023 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Now that we have increased Government involvement in the electricity market again, how would that affect or curtail the market and how will MTI and EMA ensure that electricity prices continue to remain affordable to consumers?

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure him that MTI and EMA are very mindful that the enhancement could lead to higher regulatory costs and, to mitigate this, I want to assure him and the House that we will implement the measures in a very calibrated way by balancing the cost burden while ensuring that electricity remains affordable to our consumers, households and businesses.
